rules.title: Limits on use of criminal history in tenant screening (Civil Rights Council regulations)
rules.requirement: California landlords cannot have blanket bans on applicants with criminal records, and cannot consider arrests that did not lead to convictions. Rules also limit what criminal history may be sought and how it may be used.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-record bans; no consideration of arrests without conviction
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers in California making rental housing decisions, under FEHA regulations adopted by the Civil Rights Council (formerly the Fair Employment and Housing Council).
rules.citation: California Civil Rights Council FEHA housing regulations on criminal history (Cal. Code Regs., tit. 2; specific section not cited in source)
rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.

rules.title: Source of income protection includes housing vouchers (SB 329)
rules.requirement: California landlords cannot refuse applicants because they use Section 8 or other government housing subsidies, and cannot keep "No Section 8" policies.
rules.key_value: Government housing subsidies (e.g., Section 8) are protected source of income
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing owners in California subject to the Fair Employment and Housing Act.
rules.citation: SB 329 (2019), amending Cal. Gov. Code (FEHA) definition of "source of income"
rules.quoted_span: This change meant that, as of Jan. 1, 2020, state law prohibits landlords from refusing to participate in such programs.
rules.penalty: Enforcement by California Civil Rights Department, including lawsuits.

rules.title: Credit history alternative for subsidized applicants (SB 267)
rules.requirement: If an applicant has a government rental subsidy such as Section 8, a California landlord may use their credit history only if it also offers them the option to show other verifiable, lawful proof that they can pay their share of the rent.
rules.key_value: Must offer alternative evidence option instead of credit history for subsidy holders
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental property owners in California screening applicants who receive government rental subsidies.
rules.quoted_span: to prohibit rental property owners from using a person’s credit history as part of the application process – if they have a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8 — without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.

notes: This is a secondary source (California Apartment Association compliance article), so confidence is lowered. The article does not give section numbers for the criminal history regulations, so that citation is general. For SB 267, the article only says it was adopted 'last year' and the article itself is undated, so effective_date is left null. It is generally understood to be 2024-01-01, but this document does not confirm that. HUD's 2016 federal guidance is mentioned but left out because federal rules are outside the listed jurisdictions. The article mentions no FEHA exemptions.
